questions.question: Which of the following is a key characteristic of the 'unintelligible' string of characters produced by encryption?
options: It can be easily deciphered by anyone with basic computer skills.
It is designed so it cannot be deciphered by a hacker unless they have specific means to do so.
It is only used for very short messages.
It is a temporary state before the message is deleted.
questions.answer: It is designed so it cannot be deciphered by a hacker unless they have specific means to do so.
questions.explanation: The transcript states: 'So, its un intelligible; therefore, it cannot be deciphered by a hacker or a malicious entity, unless the hacker also has ways and means to decipher it right.'

questions.question: Why is it crucial for companies to educate their website users about phishing attacks?
options: To reduce the company's marketing expenses.
Because users are the first line of defense against these attacks and can easily fall prey if unaware.
To comply with international data retention laws.
To encourage users to create more online accounts.
questions.answer: Because users are the first line of defense against these attacks and can easily fall prey if unaware.
questions.explanation: The transcript emphasizes: 'if a common user or a customer of a particular website is not familiar with what a phishing attack is, it is very easy for the user to fall prey to the phishing attack. So, therefore... most important step that a company can take today against phishing attacks is to educate website users.'

questions.question: What is the primary function of an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) when coupled with firewalls?
options: A. To encrypt all network traffic.
B. To monitor and scan for intrusions in networks.
C. To manage user access permissions.
D. To provide backup for critical data.
questions.answer: B. To monitor and scan for intrusions in networks.
questions.explanation: Intrusion detection systems are often coupled with firewalls, wherein they are used to monitor and scan intrusions in networks.

questions.question: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are characterized by which of the following features?
options: A. They work for a certain period and then stop.
B. They generate an alarm only for known viruses.
C. They feature full-time monitoring tools placed at vulnerable points.
D. They are primarily used for data encryption.
questions.answer: C. They feature full-time monitoring tools placed at vulnerable points.
questions.explanation: Intrusion detection systems feature full-time monitoring tools placed at the most vulnerable points or hot spots of corporate networks to detect and deter intruders continuously.

questions.question: If an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) detects a malicious attack, what action can it be customized to perform?
options: A. Automatically update all software on the network.
B. Shut down a particularly sensitive part of a network.
C. Send an email to all employees.
D. Initiate a full system restore.
questions.answer: B. Shut down a particularly sensitive part of a network.
questions.explanation: Once a malicious attack or security breach is detected, the intrusion detection tool can be customized to shut down a particularly sensitive part of a network if it receives unauthorized traffic.

questions.question: What is a significant limitation of most antivirus software?
options: A. They are too expensive for small businesses.
B. They are effective only against viruses already known when the software was written.
C. They slow down computer performance too much.
questions.answer: B. They are effective only against viruses already known when the software was written.
questions.explanation: Most antivirus software is effective only against viruses already known when the software was written. If there is a virus that is unknown and unique and absolutely new, antiviruses might actually fail.

questions.question: To remain effective, what must antivirus software do continuously?
questions.explanation: In order to remain effective antivirus software must be continuously updated.

questions.question: What best describes a Unified Threat Management (UTM) system?
options: B. A comprehensive appliance having various security tools in amalgamation.
C. Software designed solely for virus detection.
D. A system for managing physical security access.
questions.answer: B. A comprehensive appliance having various security tools in amalgamation.
questions.explanation: A Unified Threat Management system is a comprehensive appliance having various security tools in amalgamation.

questions.question: What are two primary benefits of implementing a Unified Threat Management (UTM) system?
options: A. Increased complexity and higher initial cost.
B. Improved manageability and reduced cost.
C. Enhanced data encryption and faster network speeds.
D. Decentralized security and increased hardware requirements.
questions.answer: B. Improved manageability and reduced cost.
questions.explanation: It is beneficial in two ways. Firstly, it improves manageability because instead of having all of these in isolation, maintenance might be very difficult – all of them are amalgamated into one product. So, maintenance becomes much easier and at the same time cost is also reduced.

questions.question: Initially, for which type of businesses were UTM systems primarily targeted?
questions.explanation: Although initially these were UTM systems were targeted at small MSMEs or small and medium sized businesses, over time they were available for all sorts of networks.

questions.question: The statement 'any information system is as secure as the security of the weakest link' emphasizes the importance of which aspect of security?
options: A. Relying solely on technological measures.
B. Focusing only on the most critical assets.
C. A comprehensive organizational approach to security.
questions.answer: C. A comprehensive organizational approach to security.
questions.explanation: It is said that any information system is as secure as the security of the weakest link. So, if there is even one weak link it can be exploited by a hacker and that can wreak havoc in the entire system. That is why it is very important to have a comprehensive organizational approach to see to manage the security.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the five steps in creating an organizational security plan?
questions.explanation: With respect to a security plan there are 5 steps. Firstly, perform a risk management develop a security policy develop an implementation plan, create a security organization and finally, perform a security audit.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of risk assessment in an organizational security plan?
options: A. To eliminate all security risks.
B. To identify which assets require protection and their vulnerability.
C. To implement new security technologies.
D. To train all employees on security protocols.
questions.answer: B. To identify which assets require protection and their vulnerability.
questions.explanation: Before a company commits resources to security, it must know which assets require protection and the extent to which these assets are vulnerable. Risk assessment determines the level of risk to the firm if a specific activity or process is not properly controlled.

questions.question: How can the expected annual loss for each exposure be determined during risk assessment?
options: A. By dividing the likelihood of a problem by the potential for damage.
B. By multiplying the likelihood of a problem by the potential for damage.
C. By adding the likelihood of a problem and the potential for damage.
D. By subtracting the likelihood of a problem from the potential for damage.
questions.answer: B. By multiplying the likelihood of a problem by the potential for damage.
questions.explanation: The expected annual loss for each exposure can then be determined by multiplying the likelihood of a problem by the potential for damage.

questions.question: A security policy primarily consists of statements that do NOT include:
options: D. Identifying mechanisms for achieving security goals.
questions.explanation: A security policy consists of statements ranking information risks, identifying acceptable security goals and identifying the mechanisms for achieving those goals or in brief it drives policies for determining the acceptable use of the firm’s information resources and which members of the company have access to those.

questions.question: If an organization identifies its email server as a highly vulnerable point, what might its security policy address regarding it?
options: A. The color scheme of the email client.
B. Who has access to the email server and password policies.
C. The number of emails an employee can send per day.
D. The type of content allowed in emails.
questions.answer: B. Who has access to the email server and password policies.
questions.explanation: For example, if you identify your e-mail server as extremely vulnerable point... then you can actually craft in your security policy who are the members of your company who would have access to that particular e-mail server. You can also set up some password related policies to protect the user IDs...

questions.question: What is the primary focus of a Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP)?
options: A. Restoring business operations after a disaster.
C. Technical issues involved in keeping systems up and running after disruption.
D. Training employees on new software.
questions.answer: C. Technical issues involved in keeping systems up and running after disruption.
questions.explanation: DRP focuses primarily on technical issues involved in keeping systems up and running, such as which files to backup and the maintenance of backup computer systems or disaster recovery systems.

questions.question: What is the main objective of a Business Continuity Plan (BCP)?
options: A. To manage daily IT operations.
B. To restore business operations after a disaster strikes.
C. To develop new security technologies.
questions.answer: B. To restore business operations after a disaster strikes.
questions.explanation: On the other hand, business continuity plan or BCP focuses on how the company can restore business operations after a disaster strikes or in other words the BCP identifies critical business processes and determines action plans for handling mission critical functions if systems go down.

questions.question: For a strong information security environment, what is stated about Disaster Recovery Plans (DRP) and Business Continuity Plans (BCP)?
options: A. They are optional for small organizations.
B. Only one of them is necessary.
C. Both plans must be in place.
D. They are only needed after a breach occurs.
questions.answer: C. Both plans must be in place.
questions.explanation: Both of these plans let me mention at the very beginning it itself have to be in place if you have to have a information security environment, a strong information security environment within your organization. These two plans are a must.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a security audit?
options: A. To install new security software.
B. To ensure that security plans and procedures work as intended.
C. To punish employees for security breaches.
D. To develop new security policies.
questions.answer: B. To ensure that security plans and procedures work as intended.
questions.explanation: You have to perform some of these mock security audits or drills to ensure that everything works you know as per the plan in case disaster strikes all of a sudden.

questions.question: A thorough security audit will often simulate what to test the response of technology and personnel?
questions.explanation: A thorough audit will even simulate an attack or disaster to test the response of the technology information system staff, and business employees.

questions.question: The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA) primarily requires financial institutions to ensure what?
options: A. Open access to all customer data.
B. The security and confidentiality of customer data.
C. The rapid processing of financial transactions.
D. The use of specific accounting software.
questions.answer: B. The security and confidentiality of customer data.
questions.explanation: This act requires financial institutions to ensure the security and confidentiality of customer data.

questions.question: What is the core focus of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) regarding patient data?
options: A. To mandate the use of paper records.
B. To ensure a balance between quality of healthcare and privacy of electronic medical records.
C. To restrict all sharing of medical information.
D. To standardize medical billing codes.
questions.answer: B. To ensure a balance between quality of healthcare and privacy of electronic medical records.
questions.explanation: It says how you know whenever there is a patient how the electronic medical records of the patients should be shared among the different entities in the health care value chain, but at the same time it should be ensured that his privacy is maintained. So, there should be a balance between the quality of health care that the customer that the patient receives and the privacy of his or her confidential electronic medical records.

questions.question: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) is fundamentally about ensuring what in financial statements?
options: B. The use of cloud-based accounting.
C. Internal controls are in place to govern the creation and documentation of information.
questions.answer: C. Internal controls are in place to govern the creation and documentation of information.
questions.explanation: SOX is fundamentally about ensuring that internal controls are in place to govern the creation and documentation of information in financial statements.

questions.question: Why does the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) require firms to consider information system security controls?

questions.explanation: Because information systems are used to generate, store and transport such data, the legislation requires firms to consider information system security controls required to ensure the integrity confidentiality availability or CIA of their data.

questions.question: What is computer forensics defined as?
options: A. The process of developing new security software.
B. The scientific collection, examination, authentication, preservation, and analysis of data from computer storage media for legal evidence.
C. The act of preventing cyber-attacks.
D. The management of network infrastructure.
questions.answer: B. The scientific collection, examination, authentication, preservation, and analysis of data from computer storage media for legal evidence.
questions.explanation: Computer forensics is the scientific collection; examination, authentication, preservation and analysis of data held on or retrieved from computer storage media in such a way that the information can be used as evidence in a court of law.

questions.question: In the context of prevention, detection, and recovery measures, what role does computer forensics play?
questions.explanation: If you consider prevention, detection and recovery measures computer forensics is a recovery measure.

questions.question: What is a key function of organizations like CERT (Computer Emergency Response and Training)?
options: A. To develop new operating systems.
B. To respond to security incidents and disseminate information about breaches and countermeasures.
D. To regulate internet service providers.
questions.answer: B. To respond to security incidents and disseminate information about breaches and countermeasures.
questions.explanation: CERT responds to thousands of security incidents each year. It helps internet users and companies become more knowledgeable about security breaches... they also post alerts to inform the internet community about security events.

questions.question: Besides CERT, which other organizations are mentioned as promoting computer security?

questions.explanation: Another example is Microsoft Security Research Group... Similarly, there are several other bodies there is some there is another body called the SANS Institute.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a technical countermeasure against security breaches?

questions.explanation: The next information security technological countermeasure pertains to intrusion detection systems.

questions.question: Why are technological measures alone often insufficient to protect organizations against security breaches?

questions.explanation: In order to protect organizations against security breaches technological measures are always not sufficient, they are not enough because they are necessary, but they not they may not be a sufficient condition because if even you know despite having n number of security technologies if there is a small loop hole the perpetrator or the hacker can easily find that out and can exploit it.

questions.question: What is the role of monitoring software within an Intrusion Detection System (IDS)?
options: A. To encrypt data before transmission.

questions.question: How have leading antivirus software companies like MacAfee and Norton enhanced their products recently?

questions.question: A Unified Threat Management (UTM) system can amalgamate which of the following security tools?

questions.question: What should information security specialists try to determine during risk assessment?

questions.question: What does a security policy determine regarding the firm's information resources?

questions.question: What does a Business Continuity Plan (BCP) identify to ensure business continues despite disruption?
options: B. Critical business processes and action plans for handling mission critical functions.

questions.question: What aspects do security audits review within an organization?

questions.question: One of the problems computer forensics deals with is recovering data from computers while preserving what?

questions.question: According to the lecture, what is considered the 'first layer of defense' against information security breaches?

questions.question: If technology is the first layer of defense, what is considered the 'next layer' against information security breaches?
questions.explanation: But, if we have to move on to the next layer of course, we have to focus on organizational policies and procedures.

questions.question: Why might antivirus software fail against a new, unknown virus?

questions.question: What challenge is highlighted in computer forensics regarding large volumes of electronic data?
